key_dates.note: Watch: SNO pipeline conversion, Forever 21 re-leasing progress
Term loan refinancing — watch spread vs SOFR

thesis_points: Quality over speed: replacing Forever 21 vacancies (~570K sqft) with experiential anchors at >2x legacy rents
New CEO Jackson Hsieh (ex-Spirit Realty) reduced ND/EBITDA from 10.8x → 7.8x within ~1 year of taking office
Crabtree acquisition: fortress-quality asset at $219/SF vs $261/SF peer, 11% going-in cap rate vs ~7-8% peers
Portfolio moat: 42 Class A malls in prime coastal metros (CA, NY, AZ, NJ, PA), $894/SF go-forward tenant sales
16 consecutive quarters of positive leasing spreads; SNO pipeline $90–140M+; new leases 9% above renewals
Deleveraging roadmap: $6.6B → ~$4.5B debt by 2029–2030, targeting ~6x ND/EBITDA via asset sales

key_debate.street: High leverage (8.2x vs SPG 5.7x, SKT 5.4x), tenant bankruptcies (Forever 21, Claire's) signal structural decline
key_debate.our_view: Occupancy gap is deliberate — quality tenants commanding >2x prior rents. Deleveraging credibly underway with $395M B/C sales in 2025

overview.narrative:
REITs posted a mixed session Thursday with defensive, long-duration names leading as the 10-year pulled back. Towers topped the leaderboard at +1.56% on average, led by SBAC +3.65%, while Healthcare was close behind at +1.51%, powered by a standout move in AHR +5.90% and WELL +4.28%. Retail (+1.37%) and Housing (+1.13%) rounded out the gainers. Office (-0.21%) and Industrial (-0.35%) lagged, with IIPR cratering -5.09% to mark the session's worst print.

The Healthcare bifurcation is notable—AHR and WELL surging while GMRE shed -1.05% underscores the market's strong preference for senior housing and growth-oriented operators over smaller medical office plays. In Industrial, IIPR's sharp decline looks idiosyncratic (cannabis REIT headwinds) against LXP's +2.23% gain, so we'd avoid reading broad sector weakness into that average. Office remains the consensus underweight, though ONL's +2.46% pop shows short-covering opportunities persist in the most beaten-down names.

Positioning into Friday should favor the momentum in Towers and Healthcare, particularly if rates remain bid. We'd watch for follow-through in SBAC and WELL as potential institutional rebalancing targets. Avoid chasing the Office bounce—FSP's -2.50% reminds us the sector's fundamental backdrop hasn't changed. Industrial deserves a closer look on any IIPR-driven dislocation.
